name: scenario_Effects_pipeline_builds_and_renders
description: The whole light pipeline from nothing: a layout says where the lights are, a layer says what they show, a driver says how the frame leaves. Builds each in turn and measures after each, so the cost of one part is the difference between two steps rather than a number with nothing to compare it to. This is the path every other light scenario assumes, which is why it is the one that builds it explicitly.

steps.name: layouts
steps.description: The container the layouts live in, which the layer reads its coordinates from.

steps.name: grid
steps.description: A 16x16 panel: small enough to run anywhere, big enough that a per-light cost is visible.

steps.name: layer
steps.description: One layer, wired to the layouts it takes coordinates from, which is what an effect renders into.

steps.name: measure-empty
steps.description: A layer with no effect: the floor every later measurement is read against.

steps.name: effect
steps.description: A gradient, chosen because it paints from the first frame: this scenario measures the pipeline rather than an effect, and an effect that needs time to develop would make a black buffer look like a broken pipeline.

steps.name: measure-rendering
steps.description: The difference against the empty layer is what one effect costs at this size.

steps.name: drivers
steps.description: The drivers container, wired to the effects whose buffer it reads, again mirroring boot.

steps.name: preview
steps.description: The preview is a driver like any other, and the one every target has.

steps.name: measure-complete
steps.description: The whole pipeline: layout, layer, effect, driver. The difference is what output costs.

steps.name: the-grid-is-what-was-asked-for
steps.description: The layout reports the size it was built with, so a later resize has something to differ from.
